tasks.title: Доска: пользователи и разрешения
tasks.statement: Вы раздаёте разрешения в oVirt: пользователь, роль и объект, на котором она задана, и действует она на этот объект и на всё, что под ним. Пять сценариев: оператор, который только запускает одну машину; администратор одного кластера, у которого нет доступа к соседнему; два пользователя с разными задачами и минимальные роли для них; разрешение, заданное не на том объекте; сети и хранилище одного дата-центра при втором дата-центре рядом. Упражнение решено, когда решены все сценарии.
tasks.hint: Разрешение действует на свой объект и на всё под ним: дата-центр, затем кластеры, сети и домены, затем хосты, затем машины на них. Вверх и вбок оно не идёт. Берите самую слабую роль, которой хватает для дела, и самый маленький объект, который это покрывает.

scenarios.title: An operator who only starts machines
scenarios.story: Anna works on the support desk. She has to start and stop web-1 when customers call, but she has no business changing its configuration, and db-1 is not hers at all. Both VMs run on the same host.
scenarios.goal: Anna can run web-1, cannot edit it and cannot touch db-1
scenarios.hint: A permission applies to the object it is set on and to everything under it. Anna needs the weakest role that can still run a VM, set on the smallest object that holds only web-1.

scenarios.title: The administrator of one cluster
scenarios.story: Boris looks after cluster-a: its hosts and the VMs on them. Cluster-b in the same data center belongs to another team, and Boris has no access to anything there yet.
scenarios.goal: Boris manages cluster-a, its hosts and VMs, and cannot touch host-3 or db-1 in cluster-b
scenarios.hint: A permission set on a cluster reaches its hosts and the VMs placed on them, but not the next cluster. Pick the role that may manage a cluster, and the cluster as the object.

scenarios.title: Two users, two different needs
scenarios.story: Dana, a junior operator, starts and stops VMs in cluster-a and nothing more. Erin patches host-1 and edits the VMs on it, but must not manage host-2 or the cluster.
scenarios.goal: Dana can only run the VMs, and Erin can manage host-1 and its VM but not the rest
scenarios.hint: Give each user the weakest role that does the job, on the smallest object that covers it. The roles differ in what they allow: a user role only runs VMs, a host administrator also edits them and manages the host.

scenarios.title: A permission on the wrong object
scenarios.story: Frank was made a cluster administrator of cluster-a, yet he can only work with host-1: the portal refuses everything on host-2 and host-3 and on the cluster itself. He must not see the networks of the data center either.
scenarios.goal: Frank manages cluster-a and its hosts and VMs, and still cannot see the data center networks
scenarios.hint: A permission applies down the hierarchy, never up or sideways, so a role set on a host stays on that host. Move the permission to the object that holds all three hosts and nothing above it.

scenarios.title: Networks and storage of one site
scenarios.story: Kira runs the networks and the storage of the Default data center. The Remote data center belongs to another team: Kira may not manage its network or its storage domain, even though both data centers share one engine.
scenarios.goal: Kira manages the networks, the storage and the hosts of Default and cannot manage anything in Remote
scenarios.hint: Networks and storage domains hang directly under the data center, not under a cluster. The role must allow managing them, and a role set on a data center stops at its border, whatever its name.
